newsitem.title: BURMA: Bomb kills daughter of Burmese official. [CORRECTED 04:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills daughter of Burmese official. [CORRECTED 04:20 GMT]

text.p: A bomb exploded in the house of one of Burma's top officials, Lieutenant-General Tin Oo, killing his daughter, sources close to the family said on Monday.

Government officials would not immediately confirm the blast, and several diplomats said they had not heard about the bombing, which the sources said occurred late on Sunday. Tin Oo is Secretary Two of the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) and Chief of Staff, Army.

"We heard there was a bomb blast yesterday night at the house of Secretary Two and his eldest daughter died because of the blast," one source close to the family told Reuters. Her name and age were not given.

Burma's military government has been on top security alert since late December when two bombs exploded at a Buddhist shrine in Burma (corrects from Bangkok), killing five and wounding 17. The government blamed the attack on the Karen National Union guerrilla group, which has denied responsibility.

Tin Oo is one of the hardliners in the government, and often gives speeches urging troops and citizens to "annihilate" anyone who opposes the government and anyone seen trying to undermine the stability of the nation.

Burma has been rocked by unrest over recent months, with rare student demonstrations in December followed by the bomb blast at the Buddhist shrine. In mid-March religious troubles began between Buddhist monks and Moslems and the government imposed a curfew in some areas and several restrictive measures in an effort to curb the violence and unrest.
